chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Rivalry with Marcelino Guerra and battles of music
summary: No heated rivals at first; people compared him to Guerra's swinging band, and they played joint dances that Machito promoted.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: ....in that time, because I was more, more determined.
Did you have any rivals then, Macho; you know, heated rivals, the way Puente and Tito Rodriguez were?
....then the people started compare us with Marcelino Guerra, because he had a good band, a good swinging

band, but no, it wasn't no rival, The people liked both bands, whatever their style was and they used to go to whatever we played. We played a lot of dances together. We had battle of music at the Grand Plaza, in Prospect Ave. and we had dances at the Odd-Fellows Temple and we had dances at the Agennon ballroom.
Did you promote all these dances?
Was this another way of assuring you that you and your men would be paid some money for your night's work?
